correctness.rationale: For all N≥0, greedy completed binary arches equal scattered-subsequence universality by the explicit last-new-letter missing-word argument. The four-state Rudin–Shapiro substitution follows directly from the digit-pair parity transition. Exact three-input-state additive profiles for four substituted blocks are initialized at level four; algebraic composition under a→ab,b→ac,c→db,d→dc alternates two tables when q doubles. This gives both dyadic formulas. Every N-prefix decomposes into \(s_2(N)\) aligned dyadic blocks, each having count discrepancy at most one from five-sixteenths of its length, giving the uniform bound and limit. Actual standalone checker proves symbolic affine identities and performs independent finite consistency scans. Scope is binary Rudin–Shapiro prefixes only; no finite sample is used as proof of the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: Scattered-subsequence universality and absent subsequences are actively studied word-combinatorial invariants. For the canonical four-state Rudin–Shapiro word the theorem determines a nontrivial exact density \(5/16\), a parity-dependent dyadic phase correction, and an all-prefix logarithmic discrepancy bound. These are structural asymptotic and exact-profile statements, not routine generic arch-count algorithms, arbitrary numerical slices or a short finite census. They provide a reusable baseline for studying absence thresholds and prefix subsequence coverage.
